symptom: Every mxcli project's docker stack was the Compose project `docker`: containers docker-db-1 / docker-mendix-1 and volume docker_postgres-data were shared, so a second app's `docker up` replaced the first app's containers and two apps used one Postgres volume
cause: docker init wrote a compose file with no top-level `name:`, and mxcli runs compose with cmd.Dir = <app>/.docker, so Compose derived the project name from the folder, which is `.docker` for every app (normalised to `docker`).
fix: Template v3 has a top-level `name:` filled in by docker init (mxcli-<sanitised app folder>). A stack's name is the key to its data, so it is chosen only when the compose file is created from nothing: --force on an existing file keeps its name: line, and on an old file with none pins the name Compose was using (COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME from the old .env if set, else the normalised folder name, `docker`) and prints how to opt in.
insight: Anything that changes a Compose project name strands the old named volumes silently (new empty volumes appear, nothing errors), so a fix to a naming default must be new-files-only and the regeneration path must read the old file before overwriting it. Also check what the regeneration overwrites besides the file: --force rewrites .env, which is where the pre-fix workaround (COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME) lived. The name goes in the stamped compose file, not .env, so a .env that is recreated by itself can never rename a stack. Verified read-only with `docker compose config` in temp dirs; no code path hardcodes container or volume names (all compose calls address services, not containers).
